topic: Nonphysical drift of single-state (LuGre-type) friction models under oscillating loads below breakaway (why simulated sheet creep is not evidence of slip)
citation: Dupont P, Hayward V, Armstrong B, Altpeter F. Single state elastoplastic friction models. IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control 47(5):787-792, 2002
task_or_setup: Analysis of single-state friction models (Dahl, LuGre) and an elastoplastic class that limits presliding drift
key_quantitative_findings: Existing single-state models exhibit a nonphysical drift when the applied force oscillates below the breakaway force, because presliding is modelled as a combination of elastic and plastic displacement; elastoplastic presliding substantially reduces the drift
limitations: Read in a search summary; no numbers for this plant
relevance_to_design: Part (c): the hold-down and the hand-on-paper contacts are LuGre contacts; the simulated sheet creeps by millimetres over a note under loads well below the hold's capacity (part c, the 'held' rows), which this property explains
transferability_reason: A property of the friction law used here
design_implication: Measure sheet slip on the bench (EXP-PL04); an elastoplastic friction law would be needed to simulate creep credibly
